newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM power division sold to consortium.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM power division sold to consortium.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) said on Friday its power division had been sold to a consortium comprising UK-based Midlands Power International Ltd and National Grid Group Plc and a team of Zambian management staff.

"The chairman of ZCCM, Luke Mwananshiku, is pleased to announce that, following the recent international tender for the sale of ZCCM assets, a consortium known as the Copperbelt Energy Consortium has been selected as the winning bidder," a company spokesman said in a statement.
The chairman of the ZCCM privatisation negotiating team, Francis Kaunda, hailed the sale of the power division as a "milestone".

"The award of the power division represents the first major electricity privatisation in southern Africa and is an important step in both the privatisation of ZCCM and the development of the mining and power sectors of Zambia, Kaunda said.

The group's power division distributes electrical power from the national grid to the operating divisions of ZCCM and also provides ancillary services such as civil and electric construction, and the inter-mine movement of materials to support production.
For the financial year ended March 31 1997, the power division's sales of electrical energy were 4.9 million megawatthours (MWh) compared to 4.8 million MWh the previous year.
"The award (of the power division) is subject to contract and the documentation is expected to be completed during the third quarter of 1997," the ZCCM spokesman said.
ZCCM's power division is the third ZCCM asset to have been sold after the Kansanshi mine, which was acquired by Cyprus Amax Minerals Co, and Luanshya/Baluba, which was bought by the Binani Group.
